thread.title: Despite all of the recent debates regarding the repatriation

author: Stone Fox Capital
title: Despite all of the recent debates regarding the repatriation
text:
Despite all of the recent debates regarding the repatriation tax including in the comments section of my previous article and forecasts of a ramped up capital return plan, Apple ( AAPL ) has so far not made any statements regarding changing existing plans. For numerous reasons, investors should want the tech giant to keep trucking along with the existing capital return plans and stick to a 'normal' dividend hike.
Repatriation Tax Hit As predicted, Apple faces a repatriation tax hit that approaches $40 billion. The company announced last week that the tech giant anticipates a $38-billion repatriation payment.
According to the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act, Apple has to pay a 15.5% repatriation tax on foreign earnings held in liquid assets like cash. Non-liquid assets are charged at an 8.0% rate with tax credits offered via some of the foreign tax paid on these earnings.
Investors should read my previous articles on the subject for the details of how Apple got to such a massive hit. The bottom line is that the company now has the ability to utilize the $269 billion cash hoard as deemed appropriate.
The company has up to 8 years to repay the $38 billion. Assuming a one-time payment, Apple would have $115 billion in net cash prior to the December quarter moves.
Apple suggests ramping up spending on capital expenditures and domestic hiring in the U.S. The company plans to spend $30 billion on capital expenditures in the U.S. and create over 20,000 new jobs in the next five years. The company spent just over $12 billion on total capex globally last fiscal year, so $6 billion annually in the U.S. suggests a total boost though nothing drastic for a company with a sales target reaching over $270 billion this year.
